relations.subject: n1ql:auto-update-statistics
relations.evidence: Optimizer statistics are crucial as they help the [Cost Based Optimizer](cost-based-optimizer.md) generate optimal query plans.

relations.subject: n1ql:auto-update-statistics
relations.evidence: This task evaluates statistics based on expiration policies to identify outdated ones and then refreshes them by running the [UPDATE STATISTICS](updatestatistics.md) statement.

notable_absence.finding: This page gates access entirely with named classic-RBAC-style roles (`query_system_catalog`, `query_manage_system_catalog`) - the same privilege model used by server/'s query-awr.md counterpart - rather than the Capella management-plane `requiresCapellaRole` gate or the Basic/Advanced `incompatibleWithCredentialType` pair seen on DDL statements elsewhere in this batch's registry. This is the same pattern already surfaced in cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-awr.json (same round): system catalog/administrative pages on Capella appear to reuse server/'s classic role-privilege model unchanged, rather than adopting the credential-type/capella-role axis that gates ordinary DML/DDL statements.

cross_component_finding: Recurrence of the known issue in docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: this page states 'AUS is available only in clusters running Couchbase Server version 8.0 or later' and further discusses migration paths for 'pre-7.6.x versions' and 'mixed clusters' with '7.6.x and 8.0 query nodes' - all framed in terms of discrete server/ version numbers despite this being a Capella page for a continuously-deployed product with no discrete version numbers.
cross_product_finding: The system:aus / system:aus_settings privilege model (query_system_catalog / query_manage_system_catalog roles) is identical in shape and wording to what was found on cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-awr.md in the same round - strong evidence that Capella's system-catalog/administrative-feature pages share a single privilege model (classic named roles) that is distinct from both the DDL-statement credential-type/capella-role model and from server/'s privilege: namespace terms already in the registry (e.g. privilege:query-manage-index). Worth reconciling whether privilege:query-system-catalog and privilege:query-manage-system-catalog should live under a shared parent distinct from the DDL-statement privilege pair.
